The overview table confirms: the 1860 schedule lists names, ages, birthplaces — **but no relationships column** (that's 1880+). Let me pull the per-year 1860 page to confirm which fields it actually collected before I construct the query.

The wiki redirected to the general page — confirmed from the summary table: the 1860 schedule records **names, ages, and birthplaces** per person, but **no relationship column** (that's 1880+) and **no parents' birthplaces**. The schedule also has a "married within the year" checkbox. Any husband/wife/child inference from this census is from listing order and surname — not a stated field. Collection ID for the 1860 census is **1473181**. Now running the search.

One result found in Bucks County, PA. Note: `relativeTerms.spouse: absent` — the index entry doesn't name Catherine directly, but her absence from the index isn't unusual for pre-1880 census entries where co-residents are partially indexed. Let me log this search and read the full record simultaneously.

The sidecar shows only Henry and Margaret as co-residents — no Catherine. Since the sidecar gives reduced co-resident facts, I'll do a live read to see the full household.

The live read confirms the household: **no Catherine** appears. The indexed co-residents are Henry and Margaret Ackerman only. Let me now present the full findings to the researcher.

---

## Search Results — 1860 US Federal Census, George Ackerman, Pennsylvania

**Logged:** log_002 · 1 result returned · ad-hoc search (no plan item)

---

### What Was Found

**Record:** United States Census, 1860 — collection 1473181
**FamilySearch ARK:** https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M7QZ-8KD
**Search score:** 0.88

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | George Ackerman |
| Estimated birth year | about 1818 |
| Birth place | Pennsylvania, United States |
| Residence (1860) | **Bucks County, Pennsylvania** |
| Indexed co-residents | Henry Ackerman, Margaret Ackerman |

---

### What the Record Shows About the Marriage — and Its Limits

**Catherine is not in this indexed household.** The search was run with `spouseGivenName: Catherine`, and FamilySearch returned this one result — but with `relativeTerms.spouse: absent`, meaning the index entry for George makes no mention of a spouse at all. The full live read of the record confirms the same: only **Henry Ackerman** and **Margaret Ackerman** appear as co-residents alongside George. No Catherine.

This means one of two things:

1. **This is the right George, but Catherine wasn't indexed.** The 1860 census is an index of an original page image, and indexers sometimes omit or mis-transcribe household members. Catherine could be on the original image page but not captured in the FamilySearch index.
2. **This is a different George Ackerman** — one who had no Catherine in his household in 1860.

**What the 1860 schedule itself can tell you about a marriage** is also structurally limited:
- ✅ The schedule records **name, age, sex, birthplace, occupation, and real/personal estate value** per person.
- ✅ It has a **"married within the year"** checkbox — but that field does not appear in the API-returned facts here, so it was either blank or not transcribed.
- ❌ **No "relationship to head" column** — that is 1880 and later. Any designation of George as "head" and Catherine as "wife" would be the indexer's inference from listing order and shared surname, not a stated fact.
- ❌ **No "years married," no marriage place, no marriage date.**

So the 1860 census, even with a confirmed household, cannot give you a marriage year or location — only a consistent co-residence pattern from which a marriage is inferred.

---

### Recommended Next Steps

Since Catherine is absent from the indexed record, I'd suggest either:

1. **View the original image.** The page scan for this Bucks County household may show Catherine where the index does not. You can visit the ARK above on FamilySearch and navigate to the image.
2. **Run record-extraction** on this record if you want to formally document George's details and the household as-found (with a negative assertion about Catherine's absence from the index).
3. **Search Pennsylvania marriage records** (civil or church) to find a George Ackerman–Catherine marriage directly — that will give you the date, place, and any additional identifying information the 1860 census cannot supply.
